answer:
RESULT — Skewness of log2(TPM+1) expression across all cell lines

Primary answer: The pooled gene-expression distribution is moderately RIGHT-SKEWED (positively skewed), with Fisher–Pearson skewness g1 ≈ 0.690 (≈0.69 to 3 s.f.) over all 1,673 × 19,138 = 32,017,874 values. It is a moderate, stable right skew with a long upper tail but WITHOUT heavy-tailed (leptokurtic) behaviour — pooled excess kurtosis is slightly negative (g2 ≈ -0.124), i.e., near-meso/platykurtic. So the correct phrasing is "moderately right-skewed, not heavy-tailed."

1) Pooled distribution (all cell lines × all genes, float64, no NaN/Inf):
- Skewness = 0.6897 (scipy.stats.skew, bias=True); Excess kurtosis = -0.1244
- mean = 2.6120, median = 2.3423, sd = 2.5048, min = -2.6232, max = 18.4369
- Quantiles: q01 = -0.0381, q05 = -0.0064, q25 = 0.0794, q50 = 2.3423, q75 = 4.4908, q95 = 6.9111, q99 = 9.2258
- Right-tail evidence is visible in the quantiles themselves: distance median→q99 (6.88) far exceeds q01→median (2.38), and q95/q99 sit 1.7/2.6 sd above the mean. 11.083% of values are negative (batch-correction artefacts, kept unclipped — the distribution is log-scaled, not raw TPM, so the skew is not a raw-count artefact).

2) Per-cell-line skewness across genes (n = 1,673 lines):
- mean = 0.694, median = 0.679, min = 0.267, max = 2.019, IQR = [0.602, 0.768]
- 100.000% of cell lines have positive skewness — right-skew is a UNIVERSAL property, not driven by a subset. No line has negative or near-symmetric skew (minimum is +0.267, comfortably positive); hence no outlier ACH- IDs to flag and no Model.csv name lookup was needed.

3) Excess kurtosis: pooled g2 = -0.124. Per-cell-line: mean = -0.062, median = -0.147, min = -0.910, max = 7.962, IQR = [-0.338, +0.100]; only 33.4% of lines have positive excess kurtosis. So the positive skew is NOT accompanied by large positive kurtosis — phrasing stays "moderate right skew, roughly normal-like tail weight (slightly platykurtic overall)," rather than "heavy-tailed."

4) Negatives retained: 11.083% of pooled values < 0 (min -2.62), noted in the script output; no flooring applied.

5) Robustness: deterministic subsample (numpy default_rng(42), 2,000,000 values without replacement) gives skewness 0.68901 vs full 0.68971 — |diff| = 0.0007, agreement confirmed; flattening/dtype handling is sound.

6) Numerical stability: input verified float64 with 0 NaN and 0 Inf; statistic computed with scipy.stats.skew(flattened float64, bias=True), and cross-checked with an independent two-pass computation (pairwise-summation mean, then m2, m3 with dtype=float64 accumulators): g1_two-pass = 0.689708, |diff vs scipy| = 0.0e+00 (assertion <1e-8 passed). No overflow or precision loss in the third central moment (m3 = 10.839).

Deliverable: single self-contained executed script analysis/skewness_analysis.py (run completed in ~14 s), console capture saved to analysis/skewness_output.txt. CRISPRGeneEffect.csv untouched; Model.csv not joined.

Concise final answer for submission: "The log2(TPM+1) expression distribution pooled across all 1,673 cell lines (32.0M values) is moderately right-skewed: Fisher–Pearson skewness ≈ 0.69 (mean 2.61 > median 2.34; long upper tail to 18.4), with no heavy tails (excess kurtosis ≈ -0.12). This is universal — every one of the 1,673 cell lines shows positive per-line skewness (median 0.68, range 0.27–2.02)."
